note: Milan evolved from a self-governing commune (from the late 11th century) to a Signoria under the Visconti family (from 1277), then to a formal duchy when Emperor Wenceslaus granted Gian Galeazzo Visconti the ducal title (1395). The commune's institutions — consuls, the podestà system — were gradually replaced by Visconti autocracy. After Filippo Maria Visconti's death (1447), a brief Ambrosian Republic (1447–1450) tried to restore communal government; Francesco Sforza's conquest (1450) created the Sforza duchy that dominated Lombardy until 1499.

_quarry.structural_significance: Milan's evolution from commune to duchy models the pattern of signorial consolidation across northern Italy; the Sforza duchy becomes the most sophisticated Renaissance court after Florence; its conquest by Louis XII (1499) opens the Italian Wars
